title: How Friday the 13th Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explore why many people fear Friday the 13th, timed to the day before the holiday. They cover the phobia paraskevidekatriaphobia, the avoidance of thirteen in floors, hotels and planes, and the Norse myth of Balder's death at a banquet of twelve with Loki as the uninvited thirteenth guest, linked to the Last Supper. They discuss Tom Harpur's book The Pagan Christ on Egyptian parallels to Christianity, the early Church's competition with pagan holidays, and the Friday associations in Christianity (the Crucifixion, Eden, the Flood). Studies of Friday the 13th traffic and hospital admissions are mentioned, along with the idea of psychological bias. The hosts list positive thirteen associations (bar mitzvah, Colgate University), unlucky numbers in other cultures (four in Japan and China, seventeen in Italy), and athletes and films tied to thirteen. They close with the Gregorian calendar and the 2009 Friday the 13th films, then a sponsor read for Audible and a listener mail correction about the Egyptian god Horus, whose falcon head was misidentified as a cat's.

segments.title: Opening sponsor read and intro
segments.summary: Opening sponsor read for a camera and Audible, followed by Josh and Chuck introducing the Friday the 13th topic at a listener's suggestion.

segments.title: Fear of Friday the 13th and avoidance of thirteen
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the phobia of Friday the 13th, paraskevidekatriaphobia, and note the avoidance of the number thirteen in building floors, hotels, planes and Little League.

segments.title: Norse myth of Balder and the Last Supper
segments.summary: Josh recounts the Norse myth in which Loki, the thirteenth guest at a banquet of twelve, kills Balder, linking it to the Last Supper and Judas.

segments.title: Pagan Christ and Egyptian parallels
segments.summary: Chuck describes Tom Harpur's book The Pagan Christ, which argues Christianity and Judaism drew on Egyptian religion, citing Horus parallels. The early Church's competition with pagan holidays and Frigga's role among witches are discussed.

segments.title: Friday's bad reputation in Christianity
segments.summary: The hosts describe Christian associations of Friday with bad events, including the Crucifixion, Adam and Eve, and Noah's Flood, and the reluctance to start projects on Friday.

segments.title: Studies on Friday the 13th and psychological bias
segments.summary: A British medical journal study found fewer people drove on Friday the 13th but more hospital admissions for car accidents. The hosts attribute this possibly to psychological bias, referencing the film Pi.

segments.title: Lucky thirteen and unlucky numbers around the world
segments.summary: The hosts cite positive thirteen associations such as the Jewish bar mitzvah and Colgate University, and unlucky numbers like four in Japan and China and seventeen in Italy.

segments.title: Athletes, films and calendar history
segments.summary: Discussion of athletes who wore thirteen (Dan Marino, Alex Rodriguez, Wilt Chamberlain), the Friday the 13th film series, Black Sabbath's debut album, and Pope Gregory's calendar change.

segments.title: Audible sponsor read
segments.summary: Sponsor read for Audible promoting a free audiobook download and recommending titles including The Maltese Falcon and Jack Kerouac's Wake Up Road novel read by David Carradine.

segments.title: Horus correction listener mail
segments.summary: Listener mail correcting an earlier mistake: Horus has a falcon head, not a cat's head, and the jackal-headed god is Anubis.
